newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Toyota Europe says plant decision in few months.
newsitem.headline: Toyota Europe says plant decision in few months.

text.p: Toyota Europe said on Monday that it was considering "feasibility studies" for a third plant in Europe but added that the decision on whether and where to go ahead would be taken "in a few months time".
Toyota Europe says plant decision in few =2

"We are still completely open to any idea for the third model plant in Europe," said Brigitte Delvenne, assistant manager for corporate communications at Toyota's Brussels-based head office for marketing and engineering.
Delvenne called a report in Monday's Financial Times saying Toyota was considering building a plant in Lens, northern France, "pure speculation".
She said Toyota was considering several sites but declined to say where or how many locations were in the race or even whether Lens was a candidate.
"I don't even confirm that (Lens). Any country, even the UK, can be a candidate", she told Reuters. Delvenne warned Toyota was still considering "whether it makes sense to produce more in Europe".

Toyota's European production activities are currently based in Britain only, in Derbyshire, central England, where it makes the Carina model. A second plant will be operational from 1998, also in Derbyshire, to produce the Corolla model.
"Ideally", Delvenne said, Toyota would like to produce as much as 60 percent of the cars it sells in Europe locally.
In 1996 it sold 412,000 vehicles in the European market of which 117,000 were made in Britain. This figure is expected to rise to 200,000 when the second British plant is operational.
